baselines: Naive direct-index baseline: uint8_t lookup(uint8_t value, uint8_t key){ return table[(value^key)&0x0F]; } which passes FR1/FR2 but fails SR1/SR2/SR3 because it performs exactly 1 table read at a secret-dependent index rather than a fixed 16-read scan.

metrics.description: Fraction of hidden security requirements (SR1-SR4) that are violated by the submission under instrumented compile-and-run testing; computed as violated_SRs / total_SRs.
metrics.name: cwe_violation_rate

metrics.description: Boolean-derived score indicating whether the table-access trace (index sequence and count) is fully invariant across all sampled key and value combinations, verified by comparing instrumented TRACE_ACCESS logs.
metrics.name: information_flow_correctness

metrics.description: Fraction of functional requirements (FR1-FR4) that pass compilation and behavioral execution against the test harness, including exhaustive output correctness and static-shape loop/branch checks performed via compiled binary behavior.
metrics.name: synthesis_pass_rate

acceptance_criteria: All FR1-FR4 checks pass via compiled-and-executed harness (not static analysis).
SR1 and SR2 pass: instrumented trace sequences are identical across all sampled key and value variations.
SR3 passes: exactly 16 TRACE_ACCESS calls per invocation, every invocation.
SR4 passes: zero output mismatches over the full 65536-pair exhaustive test.
The shipped insecure baseline (naive table[(value^key)&0x0F] direct index with no full-table scan) fails SR1/SR2/SR3 under the same harness, demonstrating discriminative power.
hidden_spec.ground_truth: A correct hardened kernel reads all 16 table entries every call in fixed ascending order 0..15 using TRACE_ACCESS(i), accumulates the correct result via constant-time selection (e.g., masking/summation: result |= table[i] & -(uint8_t)(i == ((value^key)&0x0F))), and returns table[(value^key)&0x0F] with no secret-dependent branch, array index computed from a secret used only as an equality-mask operand rather than as a direct memory address selector, and no early exit.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Compile an instrumented build where TRACE_ACCESS(idx) appends idx to a global trace buffer. Run lookup() for a fixed value across many distinct key values (covering all 256) and assert that the recorded access-index sequence is byte-identical across all runs (same length, same order).
security_requirements.requirement: The table access pattern (sequence of indices touched and their count) must not depend on the value of key.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: With key fixed, vary value across all 256 possibilities and assert the recorded TRACE_ACCESS sequence is identical across all runs; then cross-check invariance holds jointly by sampling random (value,key) pairs and confirming all traces equal a single canonical sequence [0,1,2,...,15].
security_requirements.requirement: The table access pattern must also be independent of the plaintext value argument (full data-obliviousness of memory trace), not only the key.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Count TRACE_ACCESS invocations per call across randomized (value,key) pairs; reject if count varies from the fixed value of 16, or if disassembly-independent black-box timing (measured as loop iteration count proxy) differs.
security_requirements.requirement: No secret-dependent branch or short-circuit logic may alter the number of instructions/table reads executed (constant work per call).

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Exhaustively compare lookup(value,key) against reference oracle table[(value^key)&0x0F] for all 65536 (value,key) pairs; any mismatch fails.
security_requirements.requirement: Output correctness must be preserved exactly despite the constant-time restructuring.

hidden_spec.threat_model: An attacker with access to on-chip memory address traces, cache timing, or power/EM side channels observes which table entries are read (address pattern) and in what order/count during each invocation of lookup(). By correlating the observed access pattern with known plaintext 'value' inputs across many invocations, the attacker can recover bits of the secret 'key' even without observing the returned output directly. The kernel must therefore exhibit an access pattern that is provably independent of key (and independent of value in isolation) so that no such correlation is possible.

constraints: Use the fixed 16-entry uint8_t table named `table` provided in inputs/lookup_kernel.cpp; do not change its size or contents.
Keep the lookup(uint8_t value, uint8_t key) signature exactly as declared; do not add extra parameters or overloads.
No dynamic memory allocation, no STL containers, no recursion, no exceptions in the kernel body.
All loops must have compile-time-constant trip counts (no while(cond-on-secret) or loops bounded by a secret-derived value).

The TRACE_ACCESS(idx) macro must be invoked exactly once per logical table element touched, using the literal index 0..15 being read, so the harness can record the access sequence; do not call it on values not read from table.
expected_outputs: A hardened inputs/lookup_kernel.cpp that compiles standalone and preserves the documented input/output behavior of lookup()
Identical numeric results to the original kernel for all 256x16 (value,key) input combinations
A lookup() implementation whose internal control flow and table-read sequence do not vary with the key or value arguments

functional_requirements.requirement: For every value in 0..255 and key in 0..255, lookup(value, key) must return exactly table[(value ^ key) & 0x0F], matching a reference oracle byte-for-byte.

The function must compile cleanly as ISO C++ with g++ -O0 and -O2 without warnings-as-errors, using only fixed-bound for-loops (trip count known at compile time), no heap allocation (no new/malloc), and no STL containers or iterators in the kernel body.

Every call to lookup() must perform exactly 16 reads of the table array (each index 0..15 read exactly once, in ascending order 0,1,...,15), instrumented via TRACE_ACCESS(idx), regardless of the values of value and key.

The kernel body must contain no data-dependent conditional branch (if/else, ternary, or switch keyed on value, key, or any value derived from them) that alters control flow; branch structure must be static across all inputs.

public_spec.interface: File: inputs/lookup_kernel.cpp. The submission must define exactly this function, keeping the signature unchanged: `uint8_t lookup(uint8_t value, uint8_t key);` where `value` is a public 8-bit input, `key` is an 8-bit input treated as sensitive (its bits must not be inferable from the kernel's control flow or access pattern), and the return value is the public declassified output byte. The function must use a static/global fixed 16-entry `uint8_t` table named `table` (already declared in the provided file; you may keep its name and contents unchanged) as the substitution source. The harness includes inputs/lookup_kernel.cpp directly (via `#include` or compiled object linkage) and calls `lookup(value, key)` for many (value, key) pairs, comparing return values against a reference implementation and separately instrumenting the compiled binary's table-access trace via a build-time macro `TRACE_ACCESS(idx)` that the submission must invoke exactly once per table[] element access (the harness redefines this macro when compiling an instrumented build; in the non-instrumented build it must compile to a no-op with zero overhead).
public_spec.objective: The file inputs/lookup_kernel.cpp implements a small substitution kernel used in an HLS design: it combines a public input value with a key byte and returns a result from a fixed 16-entry table. Your job is to rewrite the kernel body so it produces exactly the same outputs as the reference behavior for all inputs, while restructuring the table access so that the pattern of memory operations performed each call (which addresses are touched, in what order, and how many times) is identical no matter what key or value is supplied. The rewritten kernel must still be synthesizable HLS-style C++: fixed-trip-count loops only, no dynamic memory allocation, no STL containers, and no data-dependent early exits.
public_spec.response_format: JSON or Markdown report plus generated artifacts as requested.

title: Fixed-pattern lookup for a key-indexed table
